rationale: All modelled costs use a common 2026 real-AUD basis.
notes: Current 2026 Australian contract benchmarks require no escalation; older/transferred sources are used mainly as ratios or contextual checks.

rationale: Report whole-life cost, but interpret variant ranking mainly through differential costs because the same PV product/area is common across the 8 variants.
notes: Avoids overstating precision where BIPV product pricing is project-specific.

rationale: Australian commercial-building trajectory reference rate with 3% and 10% sensitivity.
notes: Applied to future O&M, replacement and EoL cash flows.

rationale: 2026 250-kW commercial rooftop PV capital-cost benchmark (A$310,500 / 250 kW).
notes: Context/lower-complexity benchmark only; not used as a BIPV façade price.

rationale: Transferred 2026 ClearVue commercial-project envelope: Rio Business Centre (~A$305k / >800 m²) and Canva HQ (~A$600k / >660 m²). Central is the midpoint of the two project-intensity benchmarks.
notes: Not a quote for the modelled 370-W spandrel product. Rio is glazing+framing+electrical-design supply; Canva is a mixed-product supply/install package. Used as a market-scale sensitivity envelope, not a precise unit price.

rationale: Uses the common BIPV package cost envelope without an added ventilated-substructure proxy.
notes: Maintains a transparent baseline; not claimed as a contractor quote.

rationale: Transferred proxy from a full-size ventilated BIPV façade case: additional substructure-fitting + cassette-related cost = 42.4 €/m² relative to 621 €/m² PV-façade cost (~6.8%).
notes: This is a complexity proxy, not an Australian market premium and not a pure ventilation-only effect.

rationale: Common BIPV package cost multiplied by the transferred ventilated complexity factor.
notes: Low/central/high combine the BIPV market envelope with the 3/6.83/10% factor.

rationale: No defensible Australian market premium was found, so reversibility is treated parametrically rather than asserted as a market price.
notes: 5% is only a central test point. Break-even analysis solves the maximum defensible premium directly.

rationale: Common BIPV package cost multiplied by the parametric reversibility-premium factor.
notes: Primary break-even variable, not an empirical market estimate.

rationale: Central 0.5%/yr follows the transferred BIPV LCC benchmark; NREL reports ~0.35% for a large grid-connected reference and recommends ~0.5% for large systems, with 1% a reasonable small-system expectation.
notes: 0.35/0.50/1.00% is used as a bounded O&M sensitivity, not as an Australia-specific tariff.

rationale: Initial direct-mount façade cost × common area × O&M rate.
notes: Central-case bookkeeping value.

rationale: Initial ventilated façade cost × common area × O&M rate.
notes: Central-case bookkeeping value.

rationale: Transferred BIPV LCC benchmark uses 10% of initial investment for inverter replacement at the reference replacement interval.
notes: Common to all variants, so it does not drive factorial ranking; retained for absolute WLC.

rationale: Linked to the inverter reference service life in Block C.
notes: One scheduled replacement in the 30-year horizon.

rationale: One failed product is permanently replaced per event; material cost = reference-module area × BIPV package cost.
notes: Low/central/high inherit the BIPV market envelope. Access/handling burden is not hidden in this value.

rationale: Adjacent units handled for access are not assumed to be discarded or replaced.
notes: Their burden remains in the separate replacement/disturbance criterion and break-even access-cost analysis.

rationale: No robust project-specific façade-access cost is asserted. The analysis solves the event-cost threshold at which reversibility/ selective access becomes worthwhile.
notes: This deliberately avoids converting minimum award wages into contractor/project costs.

rationale: Equivalent module count × 25.5 kg reference-product mass.
notes: Excludes substructure/BOS mass; PV-product waste basis only.

rationale: Australian PV recycling estimate including transport at approximately 500–1000 AUD/t; 750 AUD/t midpoint used centrally.
notes: Cross-check: Recycling Victoria reports ~A$28 per panel, which is of similar order for the 25.5-kg reference product.

rationale: End-of-life PV mass multiplied by the all-in Australian recycling-service cost.
notes: Transport is already embedded; do not add a separate transport charge in the baseline.

parameter: Transport share of all-in recycling cost
rationale: Recent Australian evidence estimates transport at roughly 10–15% of recycling cost.
notes: Used only to decompose/interpret the all-in recycling fee, not added again.

rationale: All-in recycling cost × transport-share assumption.
notes: Accounting decomposition only.

rationale: All-in recycling cost minus the transport component.
notes: Accounting decomposition only.

rationale: Recycling Victoria reports A$22.60 potential recovered-material value for a typical 20-kg panel (~A$1,130/t).
notes: Potential gross material value is not assumed to accrue to the building owner.

rationale: Central case assumes no owner recovery credit because revenue-sharing/take-back arrangements are not documented; upper sensitivity uses the gross potential material value.
notes: Directly supports reviewer-requested recovery-value break-even analysis.

rationale: End-of-life PV mass × owner recovery credit.
notes: Zero in the central case.

rationale: Australian recycling benchmark already includes transport, so a separate $/t-km charge would double count costs.
notes: Transport-distance sensitivity is represented through logistics/recycling-cost stress cases rather than an unsupported per-km tariff.

rationale: No defensible BIPV-specific Australian removal-cost dataset was found. Removal/access benefit of reversibility is therefore solved parametrically.
notes: Keeps the model honest rather than fabricating a site-access price.
